core.title: Give every component URN a valid layer value
core.given: A component exists or is being declared, identified by a component URN
core.when: The planner writes, edits or reviews that component URN
core.then: The component URN contains a valid layer value in its designated layer segment — a single value chosen from the profile's allowed layer-role set, spelled exactly as listed there.
prefer: Put the layer in the component URN's designated layer segment, using one value spelled exactly as in the allowed layer-role set; which segment is the layer segment is a property of the stack's component URN shape, not an additional constraint of this rule.
For reference, each layer role has a typical responsibilities profile (typical operations, consumes, produces) recorded in the profile; consult it when choosing a layer.
If a component spans layers, split it into one component per layer, each with its own URN carrying that single layer value.
avoid: Component URNs with no layer value.
Invented or synonym layer values outside the allowed layer-role set.
Assigning one component to more than one architectural layer (a component belongs to exactly one layer).
core.why: Pinning each component to exactly one layer keeps the layered architecture honest and lets the URN's layer segment be trusted as the single source of truth for where a component lives.
evidence: Each component is assigned to exactly one architectural layer.
Each component URN contains a valid layer value from the profile's allowed layer-role set.
The chosen layer is consistent with that layer role's typical responsibilities profile.
verification: Check: each component URN's designated layer segment contains a valid layer value from the profile's allowed layer-role set, spelled exactly as listed; any other value (invented or synonym) is a violation, and a URN with no layer value is a violation.

Which segment is the layer segment, and where it sits, is designated by the stack's component URN shape (profile key urn.component); that position is descriptive shape data, not a grammar requirement of this rule. The check validates the presence and exact value of the layer in that designated segment; it does not forbid identity segments whose text coincidentally equals an allowed layer value. Layer membership is read from the designated layer segment, not from incidental segment text.
Exactly-one-layer membership is a separate check: flag any component described or declared under more than one architectural layer.
Consistency of the chosen layer with that layer's typical responsibilities profile is a review judgment against the profile's reference data; it is not a mechanical value check.

The source convention declares no automated implementation for this rule (implementation type none); verification is by review. A stack may provide a URN parser/validator against the allowed layer set plus a membership observer, but the core obligation does not require one.
Non-component URNs are out of scope for this check: other artifact kinds' URNs carry no layer by design.

values: any artifact declaring component URNs (plan artifacts, acceptance artifacts, specs, docs; not limited to changed or plan-only files)
component URN with a layer value outside the allowed layer-role set
component assigned to more than one layer

fires: The planner declares a new component URN in any plan artifact
The planner edits an existing component URN or its layer value
Any component URN (new or existing, changed or not) has no layer value or uses a value outside the allowed layer-role set
A component is described as belonging to more than one layer
doesNotFire: Non-component URNs (other artifact kinds' URNs) that carry no layer by design
Work that neither declares, changes, nor inspects any component

profileRequirements.meaning: The stack's allowed layer-role values (with their local names); the core's allowed layer set for a component URN is exactly this list.
The stack's local name for the composition-root role, which is one of the allowed layer values (so the neutral role list instantiates to the Bun value set).

The component URN shape: colon-separated segments with a leading 'component' segment, and a single designated layer segment that carries the layer value. The layer segment is identified by its designated position in the stack's URN shape, not by being the only segment whose text matches an allowed layer value: identity segments are unconstrained text and may coincidentally carry a layer-like value without affecting layer membership. The layer segment's position (final segment in the Bun worked example) is stack-defined and descriptive; it is not a fixed constraint of this core.
profileRequirements.bunValue: component:<…identity segments…>:<layer> — colon-separated; first segment 'component'; the designated layer segment carries the layer value from the allowed set; which segment is the layer segment is a stack choice (in the Bun worked example it is the final segment — descriptive, not a grammar rule); identity segments are otherwise unconstrained text and may coincidentally equal an allowed layer value

profileRequirements.meaning: The concrete planning-artifact kinds that can declare component URNs. The activation scope is unrestricted (any artifact declaring component URNs); these kinds are the planning artifacts within it, mapped from the Bun enumeration.
The concrete acceptance-artifact kinds that can declare component URNs, mapped from the Bun enumeration within the unrestricted any-artifact scope.
Per-layer typical responsibilities (typical operations/methods, consumes, produces) used as reference when choosing a layer and when reviewing layer consistency.
profileRequirements.bunValue: presentation: typical methods render/handleInput/updateDisplay, consumes user interactions & display updates, produces ui events & user actions; application: typical methods execute/coordinate/validate, consumes commands & queries, produces events & responses; domain: typical methods process/calculate/applyRules, consumes domain events, produces domain events & state changes; integration: typical methods fetch/save/publish, consumes external events, produces external calls & persistence operations; assembly: no profile in source.

neutralityNotes: The allowed layer set is data, not wording: the core defers to the profile's layer-role list, where Bun's 'assembly' is the composition-root role's local name (roles.composition_root.name). The layer segment is designated, not inferred from text: the urn.component profile value is a reusable shape carrying only supported constraints (colon-separated segments, leading 'component' segment, one designated layer segment), the layer segment is identified by its position in the stack's URN shape, and identity segments remain unconstrained text that may coincidentally equal an allowed layer value without affecting layer membership — no segment-value uniqueness constraint is added. The layer-segment position stays descriptive: bun.json's additions explicitly state the final-segment placement comes from its only compliant example and is not a grammar rule, so core.prefer[0] and core.verification impose no fixed position and name no realization; the final-segment placement itself remains bunOnly realization data. The concrete artifact-kind enumeration is mapped into the profile where roles exist (roles.plan_artifact.kinds: plans, wagons, WMBTs; roles.acceptance_test.kinds: acceptances); 'component specs' and 'docs' have no role in the closed vocabulary and remain bunOnly context, while the activation scope stays unrestricted (any artifact declaring component URNs, not limited to changed or plan-only files). The per-layer typical methods/consumes/produces profiles are carried by the vocabulary's map key roles.layer_catalog (entry layer_profiles), so no key was proposed. The rule bundles two checks (URN layer-value validity in then; exactly-one-layer membership in avoid[2]/evidence[0]); both are kept so the core is no weaker, even though bun.json itself proposes splitting the membership half into planner.component.single-layer-membership. Concrete examples (the value "service", the compliant project URN, the wagon/WMBT artifact-kind names) are not repeated in the core; they remain in bun.json, which is delivered as the worked reference example. bun.json's unless is empty, and the core keeps it empty. No stack, runtime, framework, language, package manager, file suffix or path is named in the core.
